routes.name: Visa-free short stay (Schengen)
routes.summary: Citizens of the countries on Italy's official list can stay up to 90 days in any 180 days without a visa. Allowed purposes include tourism, business, transit and study. Check the official list for your passport.

other: Taiwan: only passports with an ID card number.
Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine: biometric passports only.
Serbia: passports issued by the Serbian Coordination Directorate are excluded.
EU/EEA citizens do not need a visa at all (see EU free movement rules).
Check the official EU pages for any travel authorization that applies to your trip.

sources.label: Italian MFA: countries exempt from short-stay visas

routes.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C)
routes.summary: For citizens who need a visa for stays up to 90 days. Apply at the Italian consulate if Italy is your main or only destination.

other: Passport valid 3 months past your last day in Schengen, issued in the last 10 years, with two blank pages.
Travel insurance with at least EUR 30,000 coverage for medical costs, hospitalization and repatriation.
Round-trip reservation and proof of lodging for every night.
Fee and exact rules vary by consulate. Check the Italian MFA visa site (vistoperitalia.esteri.it) for your country.

steps: Check if you need a visa on vistoperitalia.esteri.it.
Book an appointment with the consulate that covers your area.
Submit documents and pay the fee.
Wait for the decision. Applications can be filed up to 6 months before travel.

sources.label: Italian Consulate Los Angeles: Schengen visa for tourism

routes.name: Digital Nomad / Remote Worker Visa
routes.summary: National visa for highly qualified non-EU freelancers and remote employees working for non-Italian clients or employers. You then get a residence permit at the Questura.

eligibility.education: Degree, or higher professional qualification with 5 years of experience (3 years for ICT roles)
other: At least 6 months of prior work in the field.

Income must come from work performed in Italy and must be about three times the minimum income that triggers Italian healthcare contributions. The consulate page does not state the final figure, so confirm the exact amount with the consulate.
Passive income (rent, stocks, pensions) does not count.
Remote employees need a contract at or above the collective contract salary and an employer letter.
Health insurance and a registered lease in your name for the whole stay. Hotels do not count.
Rules and documents vary a bit by consulate.

stay.note: Residence permit issued for one year per the 2024 consulate page, renewable while you keep work, lodging and insurance.

steps: Prove your profession, work experience and income.
Apply at the consulate in person with a registered lease and insurance.
After arriving, apply for the permesso di soggiorno at the Questura within 8 working days.
routes.processing: Check the consulate's page for current fees and times.

sources.label: Italian Consulate New York: Digital nomad visa

routes.name: Elective Residence Visa
routes.summary: For people with stable passive income who want to live in Italy without working. Paid work is banned.

other: Income must be steady passive income (pensions, annuities, investments, rent). Work income does not count.

The consulate page says the minimum is three times the Table A amount from the 2000 Interior Ministry directive, roughly EUR 32,000 per year per applicant. This was stated loosely, so confirm the exact amount.
Proof of lodging in Italy for the whole stay (purchase or rental).

stay.note: Maximum length not stated on the page.

steps: Apply to your consulate with income and lodging proof.
Register on Prenot@mi for the fingerprint appointment.
After arriving, apply for a residence permit within 8 working days.
routes.processing: Consulate page warns national visas can take 45 to 90 business days.

sources.label: Italian Consulate Toronto: Elective residency visa

routes.name: Investor Visa (Golden Visa)
routes.summary: Residence for non-EU investors who put money into Italy. You first need a nulla osta from the Investor Visa for Italy Committee, then apply at the consulate.

investment.note: Lowest tier: innovative start-up. Other tiers: EUR 500,000 in Italian company shares or bonds, EUR 1 million in public-interest projects, EUR 2 million in Italian government bonds.

other: Duration of the visa was not stated on the consulate page.

steps: Apply for the nulla osta on the official Investor Visa portal.
Book an in-person appointment at the consulate.
Bring originals, a passport valid 2 years, and a one-way ticket reservation.

routes.name: Self-Employment National Visa
routes.summary: For professionals, entrepreneurs, managers, artists and similar self-employed people. Needs a Questura nulla osta first.

income.note: Prior-year income for professionals and entrepreneurs, per the Toronto page.

other: Nulla osta from the Italian Questura issued within the previous 90 days.
Entrepreneurs also declare resources of at least three times the minimum welfare income (the page says EUR 14,000).
Proof of suitable accommodation and a declaration from the professional body if needed.
Check quota rules, which this page does not mention.

routes.processing: Consulate page says about 45 to 90 business days.
steps: Get the nulla osta from the Questura.
Send the visa application to the consulate.
Attend the fingerprint appointment.
After arriving, apply for the residence permit within 8 working days.

sources.label: Italian Consulate Toronto: Self-employment national visa

routes.name: Work Visa under the Decreto Flussi Quotas
routes.summary: Italy sets yearly quotas for non-EU workers. The 2026 to 2028 decree allows 497,550 entries for seasonal, non-seasonal and self-employed work. The Italian employer applies for you online.

other: Applications go through the Interior Ministry ALI portal on set click days. 2026: Jan 12 seasonal agriculture, Feb 9 seasonal tourism, Feb 16 non-seasonal for cooperation-agreement countries, Feb 18 other non-seasonal.
Employers must prove no local workers are available.
Sector and nationality allocations are in the decree and circular. Check them.

steps: Employer prepares and files the request on the ALI portal on the click day.
If approved, you get a nulla osta.
Apply for the work visa at the Italian consulate.
After arriving, sign the stay contract and get the residence permit.

routes.name: National Study Visa
routes.summary: Long-stay visa for full programs at Italian institutions. Low or mid-level language courses do not qualify.

other: Acceptance letter from the school and a letter from the Italian institution to the consulate.
Health insurance for the whole program and proof of lodging.
Proof of funds: bank letter, parent affidavit, or institutional aid letter. The amount was not stated.
Length of stay and work rights while studying were not stated on the page.

steps: Book on Prenot@mi.
Submit documents and fingerprints.
After arriving, get the permesso di soggiorno within 8 days.

sources.label: Italian Consulate Los Angeles: Study visa

routes.name: Working Holiday Visa
routes.summary: Italy has working holiday deals with some countries. The Sydney consulate page confirms the Australian version. Other partner countries were not verified here.

savings.note: For 365 days. Reduced proportionally for shorter stays.

other: Never held an Italian working holiday visa before.
Return ticket or funds for one, plus health cover.
Other partner countries (for example Japan, Canada) exist but were not confirmed on pages I opened.

sources.label: Italian Consulate Sydney: Working holiday visa

routes.name: Family Visa for Relatives of EU/EEA Citizens
routes.summary: Spouse, dependent children under 21 and dependent parents of an EU/EEA citizen living in Italy can get a free national visa. Other family routes were not verified.

other: Proof of the relationship with apostille and translation.
Letter from the EU citizen with the Italian address.
Visa is free of charge per the consulate page.
Routes for relatives of non-EU residents were not covered by pages I could open.

steps: Apply at the consulate with relationship proof.
After arriving, get the permesso di soggiorno within 8 days.

sources.label: Italian Consulate Los Angeles: Family visa

routes.name: Citizenship by Residence (Naturalization)
routes.summary: Standard route is 10 years of legal residence, then an application to the Prefettura. Shorter periods apply to some groups.

other: Income requirement over the last 3 years (amount not confirmed here).
Shorter periods: 3 years for people with Italian ancestors up to second degree or born in Italy, 4 years for EU citizens, 5 years for refugees and stateless people.
Clean criminal record.

citizenship.note: Italian law allows multiple citizenships. Your other country may not.

steps: Live legally in Italy for the required years.
Pass B1 Italian or hold a qualifying diploma.
Apply online through the Prefettura citizenship portal.

sources.label: Italian Embassy Nicosia: citizenship by residence

routes.name: Citizenship by Marriage or Civil Union
routes.summary: Spouses of Italian citizens can apply after 2 years of marriage if living in Italy, or 3 years if living abroad. Periods are halved with minor children.

other: Marriage must be registered in Italy.

citizenship.note: 3 years if living abroad. Halved with minor children. The Stockholm embassy page quoted 48 months of processing.

sources.label: Italian Embassy Stockholm: citizenship by marriage

routes.name: Citizenship by Descent (Jure Sanguinis), 2025 Rules
routes.summary: Since Decree-Law 36/2025 (Law 74/2025), people born abroad with another citizenship only qualify through a parent or grandparent who held only Italian citizenship, or a parent who lived in Italy 2 straight years after naturalizing. Great-grandparent claims ended.

other: Parent or grandparent holds, or held at death, only Italian citizenship. No further back.
Or an Italian parent lived in Italy at least 2 consecutive years after acquiring citizenship and before your birth.
Or you applied or had an appointment by 11:59 PM Rome time on March 27, 2025, or got a court ruling on a case filed by then.
Descent through the mother counts only for births from January 1, 1948.
Apply through your consulate via Prenot@mi.
